- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast slightly to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 2.0x recent mean), model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 1.5x prior peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; apply sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% prior, 30% new sentiment) for next 5 days.
- Model underestimates in low-sentiment periods with high volatility; add 10–20% buffer if sentiment < 0.33 and 3-day std dev > 0.2.
- For long horizons (>15 days), model shows mean reversion bias; apply exponential decay to forecast weights (α=0.8) based on sentiment stability.
